title: Israel as the creators' chosen and descended people
statement: Per the canon, the people of Israel were the humans made by the creator team whose laboratory lay in the land now called Israel; at a competition among the creator teams they were judged the most successful terrestrial type 'in intelligence and genius', which the canon gives as the origin of Israel's chosen-people self-understanding; through the unions of the sons of Elohim with the daughters of men that population became the Jewish people, whom the canon calls the creators' 'direct descendants on Earth' — the canon reconciling its two statements tentatively ('peut-être'), in Raël's commentary voice answering a reader's question (LWTE-1:17-18); and the canon narrates Israel's history as a tutelage and its keeping of the biblical record as custodianship of the message. The corpus records this as canon-explicit and mainstream-unendorsed.

includes: The election-by-competition clause as the canon states it: the people of Israel 'élu par le jury scientifique comme le type humanoïde terrestre le plus réussi sur le plan intelligence et génie', given as the origin of the chosen-people self-understanding (TBWTT-2:43)
The descent clause as the canon states it: the Jews as the creators' direct descendants, through the sons-of-Elohim / daughters-of-men unions of Genesis 6 (ETTMTTP-2:104, 2:123)

The canon's own harmonization of the two clauses, carried with its hedge: the laboratory-made people of Israel, 'peut-être' because they were the most successful, became the Jewish people through those unions (LWTE-1:17-18); the record presents no single settled genealogy
The custodial clause: a message entrusted to Israel and kept rather than spread, and the Bible preserved by the Jewish people as testimony (TBWTT-4:35, 5:25, 5:31; ETTMTTP-2:124)

The tutelage arc at the canon's level — liberation and guidance (TBWTT-3:9-10), dispersion as sanction (TBWTT-3:140-142), recovery of the land as a sign of the age (TBWTT-3:225, 5:24-25) — cross-referring woh-claim-0017 (Babel) and woh-claim-0006 (the Persian and Greek emissaries) rather than restating them

The scope convention: the historical ʿIvrim ('Hebrews') are treated in public prose as incidental, cited history; the canon itself speaks of 'le peuple d'Israël', 'les Juifs', and 'le peuple élu', and this record asserts nothing about the ʿIvrim beyond the canon's own Israel line
excludes: Any population-genetic claim; no genetic evidence is asserted, and 'genetic descendants' is not the canon's wording

Any biological-superiority or individual-worth claim; 'race' (TBWTT-2:43; LWTE-1:18) is the canon's 1970s wording, not a corpus category, and the election clause is recorded as the canon's account of a self-understanding, not as a ranking the corpus endorses
Identity between the canon's 'people of Israel' and the historical ʿIvrim, the habiru/ʿapiru, or any archaeological population, beyond what the canon states

The conditional statements about the State of Israel (ETTMTTP-2:104, 2:122-127: the embassy demand, the threatened chastisement and destruction), which belong to the conditionality of woh-claim-0015 and woh-claim-0016
Jewish election theology (Deuteronomy 7:6-8 and its tradition), preserved in its own voice and not superseded by the canon's account
Watcher and Nephilim identity questions, which are woh-claim-0012's; Eden geography, which is woh-claim-0018's; Babel mechanics, which are woh-claim-0017's

alternatives.statement: Deuteronomy 7:7-8 grounds Israel's election explicitly in love and oath, 'not because ye were more in number'; the Hebrew Bible's own theory of election is non-meritocratic, and the competition reading inverts it. Modern Jewish and biblical scholarship on election (Kaminsky; Levenson; Novak) develops the same non-meritocratic reading.

Mainstream archaeology derives Israel from an Iron Age I highland population largely continuous with Canaanite culture, first attested outside the Bible on the Merneptah stele (late 13th century BCE); no lineage reaches back to a primordial creation.

The canon's two accounts — an elected laboratory population and the descendants of the unions — were read as contradictory by the canon's own readers (LWTE-1:17), and the canon's harmonization is explicitly tentative; no single genealogy can be presented as the canon's settled position.
The canon's emphasis on Israel tracks the movement's Israel-embassy strategy and the founder's account of his Jewish paternity (TBWTT-1:46; ETTMTTP-1:7) rather than independent memory.
Ranking peoples by 'intelligence and genius' has a harmful reception history whatever its intent; any public projection of the election clause carries that risk and needs explicit containment.

revision_triggers: Claim woh-claim-0001, woh-claim-0012, or woh-claim-0018 is revised or retired.
Fuller canonical text, including Raël titles not yet in the project digitization, changes the canon's harmonization of the election and descent clauses.
Public prose drifts toward genetic, superiority, or individual-worth language, or presents a single settled genealogy, all of which this record excludes.
Public prose identifies the historical ʿIvrim with the canon's people of Israel beyond the canon's own statements.
